topic: Generic characteristic-kernel cover-ratio recovery from one unknown-target perfect intervention per latent node. For every finite labeled DAG G and derivative-sign vector s, work in the relative product C2 topology on positive normalized C3 conditional mechanisms and perfect-intervention densities on [0,1], with faithful observational law and arbitrary shared C2 diffeomorphic mixing. With observable ratios R_i=dP^i/dP^0 and D_ji the Gaussian-kernel MMD between Law_0(R_i) and Law_j(R_i), prove that positive D_ji on every ancestral cover is open dense in every nonempty DAG/sign stratum. Derive the ancestral order from the ratio graph, componentwise coordinates by conditional ranks, the target assignment and exact faithful DAG by parent pruning, plus sample-split MMD confidence edges and conditional-CDF coordinate rates. Use the certified 1->2 plus isolated-3 witness with p2(y|x)=1+0.1(2x-1)(2y-1) and q_i(z)=4exp(4z)/(exp(4)-1). ROPES is the protocol consumer only after adopting a compliant positive common-support intervention generator. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Normalized affine interpolation toward a sparse edge witness preserves normalization globally and positivity, fixed derivative signs, and faithfulness locally. The direct-edge second-moment contrast is analytic and nonzero at the endpoint, so its zeros are isolated; this derives open-dense direct-edge separation and therefore characteristic-kernel cover separation. The sparse witness has an analytic moment gap above 3e-4 and Gaussian MMD above 5e-8. Exact faithful cancellation families, isolated nodes, multiple roots, forks, colliders, opposite parent effects, redundant edges, and disconnected admissibility strata were checked; no current-literature collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform conditional-CDF coordinate rates when both response thresholds and conditioning covariates are estimated log-density ratios on an explicitly bounded Holder subclass. EARLY KILL TEST: Independently verify the analytic moment-integral identity along the normalized affine path from the exact cancellation example to the sparse witness, including preservation of finite positive faithfulness and derivative-sign margins near its start. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_crl_coverratio_mmd_genericity.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Does one unknown-target perfect intervention per latent node generically identify the ancestral order, componentwise latent coordinates, intervention-target permutation, and exact faithful DAG for every finite nonlinear DAG under arbitrary shared diffeomorphic mixing?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves one-intervention-per-node identification only for two latents and explicitly conjectures the n>2 result, naming the n!-1 target misalignments as the obstacle.
source_refs.author: Julius von Kügelgen, Michel Besserve, Wendong Liang, Luigi Gresele, Armin Kekić, Elias Bareinboim, David M. Blei, Bernhard Schölkopf

source_refs.claim: For general transformations the paper establishes identification from two stochastic hard interventions per node, while one per node is obtained only with linear mixing.
source_refs.author: Burak Varıcı, Emre Acartürk, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Abhishek Kumar, Ali Tajer

source_refs.claim: Full recovery under nonparametric mixing is obtained for additive-Gaussian or heteroscedastic latent models using derivative-based change conditions, not for arbitrary positive conditional mechanisms with one perfect intervention per node.
source_refs.author: Ignavier Ng, Shaoan Xie, Xinshuai Dong, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest paper states the arbitrary-n, one-intervention-per-node result as a conjecture because its bivariate genericity witness does not directly exclude all n!-1 wrong target permutations. Paired-intervention arguments evade this combinatorics, known-graph CauCA supplies the order rather than recovering it, and general-environment results impose restrictive additive or heteroscedastic mechanisms. A cover-ratio proof must instead verify that normalized mechanism perturbations stay in each faithful sign stratum, that the ratio-law contrast is analytically nontrivial on every direct edge, and that the resulting observable graph jointly rules out every wrong target assignment.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An open-dense identification theorem in the relative product C2 topology, with an explicit ratio-graph decoder for order, componentwise coordinates, target labels, and the faithful DAG plus a sharp cancellation example on the exceptional set.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the closest nonparametric setup, the two-variable theorem, and the explicit arbitrary-n conjecture.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: nonlinear mixtures hide causal variables -> unknown perfect interventions can break representation ambiguity -> two-node genericity makes one intervention per node sufficient -> arbitrary n requires an observable certificate against every target misalignment

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the change-of-variables density-ratio equations and the bivariate witness-function argument excluding fine-tuned target swaps.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves the exact two-variable analogue and formulates the same arbitrary-n destination.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt interpolation of conditional kernels and continuity of conditional-independence constraints to establish open-density inside a nonparametric Bayesian-network topology.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed genericity proof also perturbs normalized conditional mechanisms, but must additionally control deterministic ratio laws under surgically related environments.

method_exemplars.technique: Port the deterministic perturbation-to-recovery-probability step, replacing score-variation errors under linear mixing by estimated ratio-law and conditional-rank errors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest finite-sample CRL theorem linking estimated interventional contrasts to graph and representation recovery.

open_problems.open_problem: What uniform rate and asymptotic expansion hold for conditional-CDF rank coordinates when both response thresholds and conditioning covariates are sample-split estimated log-density ratios on a bounded Hölder class?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves bias, rate, and asymptotic-linear expansions uniformly in threshold and observed covariate for local-linear conditional-CDF estimators.
source_refs.author: Haitian Xie

source_refs.claim: The paper derives rates and stochastic expansions for nonparametric mean regression with generated covariates, but not a threshold-indexed CDF with a generated response.
source_refs.author: Enno Mammen, Christoph Rothe, Melanie Schienle

source_refs.claim: The paper gives a uniform expansion for partial-mean processes with a generated regressor, not a conditional CDF whose indicator threshold and conditioning argument are both generated ratios.
source_refs.author: Ying-Ying Lee

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing results cover complementary pieces: uniform conditional-CDF theory treats observed thresholds and covariates, while generated-covariate theory linearizes perturbations of kernel weights for smoother regression targets. Here the same first-stage log-density-ratio error moves a discontinuous indicator threshold and the conditioning neighborhoods simultaneously. Sample splitting removes own-observation dependence but does not control boundary crossings of the indicator or random perturbations of local design density, so the fixed-input empirical-process and bias expansions must be replaced.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A high-probability uniform sup-norm rate and uniform asymptotic-linear representation over thresholds, conditioning points, nodes, and environments, with explicit first-stage Hölder remainders and a corollary for conditional-rank coordinate error.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly motivates simultaneous uniformity in response thresholds and conditioning values for downstream procedures.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: conditional ranks require an estimated full conditional law -> pointwise CDF theory is insufficient -> uniformity in threshold and covariate supplies downstream control -> generated ratio thresholds and covariates require a joint perturbation theorem

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the Euclidean-class entropy bound, uniform bias expansion, and asymptotic-linear representation for local-linear conditional CDFs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact threshold-indexed process before first-stage inputs become generated.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the stochastic expansion that linearizes kernel-regression perturbations caused by nonparametrically generated covariates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Estimated log-ratio conditioning variables enter the second stage in the same generated-covariate position.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the decomposition separating generated kernel arguments from their contribution to an indexed regression process.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its uniform process analysis is the nearest econometric template for propagating a nonparametric first stage through a distributional target.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp local minimax sample-complexity and simultaneous-confidence frontier for ancestral-order recovery when the minimum cover MMD tends to zero and every density ratio is learned on independent folds?

source_refs.claim: The foundational MMD paper gives deviation and asymptotic tests for two observed samples and establishes that characteristic-kernel MMD vanishes exactly at equality in distribution.
source_refs.author: Arthur Gretton, Karsten M. Borgwardt, Malte J. Rasch, Bernhard Schölkopf, Alexander Smola

source_refs.claim: MMDAgg gives nonasymptotic level control and adaptive minimax separation for observed samples, without plug-in density-ratio observations or graph-wide recovery.
source_refs.author: Antonin Schrab, Ilmun Kim, Mélisande Albert, Béatrice Laurent, Benjamin Guedj, Arthur Gretton

source_refs.claim: The finite-sample CRL analysis treats score variation with linear mixing and soft interventions, not learned likelihood-ratio laws under arbitrary nonlinear mixing.
source_refs.author: Emre Acartürk, Burak Varıcı, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Ali Tajer

source_refs.excerpt: the explicit score-Jacobian learner and attainable sharp exponent remain open
Extend the mirror calculation to a nontrivial normalized tangent class and state a uniform lower/upper comparison

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature calibrates MMD when test inputs are observed and gives finite-sample CRL guarantees for linear score contrasts; the prior SCORE proposal separately shows that a pointwise opposite-order path is not a sharp recovery frontier without a normalized tangent class and an attainable learner. In the ratio graph, plug-in errors perturb both samples through a learned function, all ordered edge decisions share fitted ratios, and recovery is nonregular as the minimum cover discrepancy vanishes. The missing proof couples least-favorable opposite-order SCM paths to a uniform learned-ratio expansion, then matches that lower bound with a specified multiple-edge selector and data-driven radius.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching minimax lower and upper bounds for order-error probability or required sample size as functions of the shrinking cover-MMD margin and density-ratio nuisance rate, together with familywise-valid confidence edges attained by a specified sample-split graph selector.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the transition from population CRL identification to a margin-dependent finite-sample recovery guarantee.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: population interventional contrasts identify causal structure -> estimated contrasts create margin-dependent errors -> fixed-separation consistency hides the near-nonidentifiable regime -> derive the sharp learned-ratio MMD recovery frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze the MMD statistic under null, fixed alternatives, and local alternatives, then lift its edgewise error control to the ratio graph.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The order margin is directly the minimum of characteristic-kernel two-sample discrepancies over ancestral covers.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt nonasymptotic calibration and minimax separation analysis across a collection of kernels, conditional on first-stage ratio fits.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination needs honest simultaneous decisions and power under a shrinking quantitative separation margin.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct least-favorable opposite-structure paths and expand their Chernoff information for a binary-testing lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Any local order-recovery converse reduces on a two-structure subexperiment to distinguishing product measures near a common cancellation law.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the maximal identifiable equivalence class from one unknown-target soft atomic intervention per node under arbitrary nonlinear latent mechanisms and arbitrary shared diffeomorphic mixing?

source_refs.claim: The paper says soft interventions may yield only transitive-closure or grouped-variable recovery and calls for a precise characterization of weaker nonparametric identifiability notions.
source_refs.author: Julius von Kügelgen, Michel Besserve, Wendong Liang, Luigi Gresele, Armin Kekić, Elias Bareinboim, David M. Blei, Bernhard Schölkopf

source_refs.claim: Soft interventions give recovery only up to mixing with parents for general latent causal models, with stronger graph recovery requiring additional nonlinearity structure.
source_refs.author: Burak Varıcı, Emre Acartürk, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Abhishek Kumar, Ali Tajer

source_refs.claim: The paper characterizes a sound-and-complete Psi-Markov equivalence class for unknown-target soft interventions on observed graphical systems, but not nonlinear latent representation recovery.
source_refs.author: Amin Jaber, Murat Kocaoglu, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Elias Bareinboim

open_problems.why_unsolved: Perfect interventions delete parent dependence, making the observational/interventional likelihood ratio an own-coordinate object; a soft mechanism change retains parent dependence, so this factorization is the first step that fails. Existing nonlinear-mixing results consequently leave parent or ancestor mixing ambiguities, whereas the sound-and-complete Psi-Markov result assumes the causal variables are observed. The missing object must simultaneously quotient nonlinear representation transformations, unknown target assignments, and the invariances of parent-dependent mechanism changes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient equivalence-class characterization of the observed multi-environment laws, with a sound-and-complete recovery map and explicit indistinguishable latent-model counterexamples at every unresolved ambiguity.

writing_exemplar.why: Its formulation makes soft changes, unknown targets, and maximal recoverability the central objects.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: real interventions alter mechanisms without revealing targets -> environment invariances contain causal information -> those invariances determine only an equivalence class -> nonlinear latent representations require the corresponding maximal class

method_exemplars.technique: Lift the Psi-Markov invariance characterization and its soundness/completeness proof from observed variables to latent-coordinate sigma-fields.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the structurally analogous unknown-target soft-intervention equivalence problem before nonlinear mixing is introduced.

method_exemplars.technique: Use score-change support and minimal-variation arguments to characterize parent-mixing ambiguities left by soft interventions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest nonlinear latent-model result that distinguishes graph recovery from representation recovery up to parents.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its concentration and perturbation argument for finite-sample recovery up to ancestors under soft interventions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its finite-sample target is a soft-intervention CRL equivalence class, although under linear mixing.

open_problems.open_problem: If scalar latent nodes are replaced by unknown innovation-atomic multivariate blocks, do intervention-ratio laws identify a unique block partition, ancestral order, target assignment, and block DAG under arbitrary within-block diffeomorphic mixing?

source_refs.excerpt: Arbitrary-block crossing rigidity and strict-refinement rigidity remain separate open obligations
arbitrary crossings and externally parented refinements remain open

open_problems.why_unsolved: The scalar cover-ratio construction uses strict own-coordinate monotonicity and a one-dimensional conditional probability transform; an arbitrary within-block diffeomorphism has no canonical componentwise rank inverse. Competing blockings may also cross or strictly refine one another while preserving the observed laws. The prior GANM run excludes only special crossings and parent-closed refinements and names the general rigidity obligations as open, so the first new proof step is a multivariate conditional-transport invariant compatible across overlapping candidate blocks.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a theorem recovering the unique innovation-atomic block partition and block DAG from ratio-law invariants under explicit discrepancy conditions, or a smooth positive same-law counterexample characterizing the crossed-block nonidentifiability frontier.

writing_exemplar.why: Its separation of supplied-group identification, causal ordering, and edge pruning is the right narrative, with unknown-block recovery inserted as the missing first stage.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: vector additive-noise asymmetry identifies a DAG when groups are supplied -> applications may not supply the causal grouping -> crossed or refined groups create ambiguity -> interventions must recover both atomic blocks and their DAG

method_exemplars.technique: Localize a graph disagreement by nondescendant conditioning and reduce it to a two-factorization additive-noise contradiction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An arbitrary-block proof must similarly isolate a minimal crossing without conditioning through a competing innovation block.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate characteristic-kernel joint-independence functionals and calibrate permutation tests for candidate residual blocks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After population block recovery, statistical pruning requires simultaneous tests of the independence restrictions defining atomic innovations.

literature_map:
1. von Kügelgen et al. (NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2306.00542) prove one perfect intervention per node only for two latents and explicitly conjecture the arbitrary-n extension.
2. Their stated obstruction is combinatorial: n!-1 wrong target alignments; their arbitrary-n theorem instead assumes paired distinct interventions per node.
3. Varıcı et al. (JMLR 2025, arXiv:2402.00849) also need two hard interventions per node under general transformations, although one suffices under linear mixing.
4. Buchholz et al. (NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2306.02235) recover linear-Gaussian causal representations under general nonlinear mixing from unknown single-node interventions.
5. Jiang and Aragam (NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2306.02899) use at most one unknown intervention per hidden variable in a measurement model, with a distinct isolated-edge orientation frontier.
6. CauCA (NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2305.17225) obtains one-perfect-intervention component recovery when the graph and target alignment structure are supplied.
7. Ng et al. (AISTATS 2025, PMLR 258) obtain nonparametric-mixing recovery from general environments by imposing additive-Gaussian or heteroscedastic latent mechanisms.
8. Jaber et al. (NeurIPS 2020) characterize Psi-Markov equivalence for unknown-target soft interventions on observed systems, leaving the nonlinear latent analogue open.
9. Squires, Wang, and Uhler (UAI 2020, arXiv:1910.09007) characterize unknown-target interventional equivalence classes when variables are observed.
10. Acartürk et al. (NeurIPS 2024, DOI 10.52202/079017-1243) give finite-sample CRL guarantees for linear mixing and score changes, not nonlinear learned-ratio graphs.
11. Boeken, Forré, and Mooij (arXiv:2410.16004) prove open-dense faithfulness by conditional-kernel topology and interpolation, but do not control surgical likelihood-ratio laws.
12. Gretton et al. (JMLR 2012) and Schrab et al. (JMLR 2023) provide characteristic-MMD identification and minimax-calibrated tests for observed samples.
13. Xie (Statistics & Probability Letters 2023, arXiv:2112.08546) establishes uniform conditional-CDF rates for observed thresholds and covariates.
14. Mammen-Rothe-Schienle (Annals of Statistics 2012, arXiv:1207.5594) and Lee (arXiv:1811.00157) propagate generated-covariate error, but not jointly generated thresholds and conditioning ratios.
15. No searched paper combines arbitrary-n cover-ratio genericity, conditional-rank recovery, and graph-wide inference under arbitrary shared diffeomorphic mixing.
